parts.title: READING PASSAGE 1
passage: Marie Curie is probably the most famous woman scientist who has ever lived. Born Maria Sklodowska in Poland in 1867, she is famous for her work on radioactivity, and was twice a winner of the Nobel Prize.

From childhood, Marie was remarkable for her prodigious memory, and at the age of 16 won a gold medal on completion of her secondary education. Because her father lost his savings through bad investment, she then had to take work as a teacher.

In 1891 Marie went to Paris and began to study at the Sorbonne. She often worked far into the night and lived on little more than bread and butter and tea. It was in the spring of 1894 that she was introduced to Pierre Curie.

Their marriage in 1895 marked the start of a partnership that was soon to achieve results of world significance. Following Henri Becquerel's 1896 discovery of a phenomenon Marie later called 'radioactivity', she decided to find out if it existed in other elements. She discovered that it did, in thorium.
parts.instructions: Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information given in the text, choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

questions.prompt: Marie Curie's husband was a joint winner of both Marie's Nobel Prizes.
Marie was able to attend the Sorbonne because of her sister's financial contribution.
Marie Curie discovered that thorium was radioactive.
According to the passage, why did Marie start working as a teacher?
options: She wanted independence from her family
Her father lost his savings in a bad investment
She had failed her Sorbonne entrance exam
questions.answer: Her father lost his savings in a bad investment
